outcome: Lumbar paravertebral muscle (LPVM) properties (contractile, biomechanical, and viscous properties: tone, relaxation time, creep, stiffness, elasticity)
cohort: The study included 30 females who experienced Cesarean birth and moderate-severity NSLBP (cases) and 30 healthy females with no prior pregnancy and no or mild-severity NSLBP (controls).
finding: Post-Cesarean birth mothers with moderate-severity NSLBP showed significant changes in LPVM contractile and viscous properties (decreased tone, increased viscosity), but not in biomechanical properties like stiffness and elasticity, compared to controls.
mod_finding: The study revealed that mothers who underwent Cesarean birth and experienced moderate-severity low back pain exhibited notable changes in their lumbar paravertebral muscle properties, emphasizing the impact of Cesarean birth on musculoskeletal health.
cross-section timing: At an unspecified time point after Cesarean birth
